assessment.nobel_worthiness: A direct discovery from nature: a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, found with a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice, opened neutrino astronomy and later linked neutrinos to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. It is exactly the kind of clue from the sky that the field cannot get by thought alone.
assessment.attribution: The credited list has one name. Halzen conceived and led IceCube, but the discovery rests on a large collaboration and on earlier detector pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, ANTARES); whether a single laureate is a fair configuration is a real question for the committee.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of the diffuse flux comes through several analysis channels and the source identifications have strengthened over a decade. The interpretation of sources is still developing but the discovery itself is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Whether recognition should be shared with other pioneers of high-energy neutrino detection (as I recall, not verified here).
Source population of the diffuse flux is still not fully understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, then observing it in HgTe quantum wells, created a new paradigm of topological band matter with large conceptual reach and many descendants. Clear, original, lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental demonstration (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction for HgTe, who are not in the supplied credit). Hasan's 3D materials work is a fourth credited name, so the allocation is contested and I choose the theory-plus-first-observation trio.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent experiments (HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3 with ARPES and transport); the interpretation is stable, and the field has been mature for over a decade.
uncertainties: Fair allocation between Molenkamp and Hasan for the experimental side.
Omitted contributors outside the supplied credit list, such as the HgTe theory predictors, complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurement of the last unknown mixing angle theta13, found to be large, made leptonic CP violation and mass-ordering searches possible. It is a clean, decisive measurement of a fundamental parameter of the Standard Model extension.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) established the nonzero value with high significance by reactor disappearance, while T2K (Nishikawa) showed first indications through appearance; Double Chooz and RENO also contributed. The credit is spread over collaborations and the trio is defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several reactor and accelerator experiments, now measured precisely. Mature, though the 2015 prize on oscillations already recognised neighbouring physics.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2015 neutrino oscillation prize may reduce urgency.
Fair credit among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magnetar model explains soft gamma repeaters and anomalous X-ray pulsars as neutron stars with fields around 10^14-10^15 gauss. It shows matter and fields in a regime no laboratory can reach, with the 2020 Galactic fast radio burst from SGR 1935+2154 adding to its reach.
assessment.attribution: Duncan and Thompson proposed the theory; Kouveliotou's observations established the field strength through spin-down measurements. This is a natural theory-plus-observation configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well supported by decades of X-ray and gamma-ray data and by the FRB connection; some details of the engine remain debated but the core picture is stable.
uncertainties: Role of earlier proposals and other observers (Paczynski, Usov and others, as I recall) in credit.
Whether magnetars explain the full fast radio burst population is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, predicted by Bistritzer and MacDonald and followed by correlated insulators and superconductivity in the Jarillo-Herrero experiments, launched twistronics and moire materials. A real discovery from experiment guided by a sharp prediction.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's 2018 experiments revealed the phases. Andrei's contemporaneous experimental work is also credited, so the choice among experimentalists is a judgment.
assessment.maturity: Many groups reproduced the phases, but the origin of superconductivity is still debated; timing is plausible but the physics is not yet settled.
uncertainties: Sample dependence and reproducibility across devices.
Credit relative to Eva Y. Andrei and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new band of the gravitational-wave spectrum and a probe of supermassive black-hole binaries or exotic early-universe sources. A clue from nature of the kind I value.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio represent pulsar timing array pioneers across NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA, but the result is a large multi-collaboration effort and the decisive individuals are hard to isolate.
assessment.maturity: Evidence in 2023 is at a few sigma and the spectrum, anisotropy and Hellings-Downs curve need further data; recognition now would be premature relative to LIGO-style detection.
uncertainties: Significance below the five-sigma standard in individual arrays.
Distribution of credit across three collaborations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness and horizon problems and, through quantum fluctuation seeds (Mukhanov), the pattern of CMB anisotropies and structure. It is a deep idea about our place in the universe, and its fluctuation predictions have been tested.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed it, Linde fixed the graceful exit and chaotic inflation, Mukhanov computed structure from quantum fluctuations; Starobinsky and Sato are not in the supplied credit, which hampers a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: The basic features (near scale-invariance, flat universe) agree with CMB data, but the inflaton, primordial gravitational waves and alternatives remain untested. As a theorist wary of beautiful ideas without confirmation, I find this not yet decisive.
uncertainties: Credit omitted for Starobinsky and Sato.
Model degeneracy in the inflationary paradigm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray and optical afterglows settled the cosmological distance of gamma-ray bursts and opened the way to studying them as probes of the distant universe and of massive-star death. A clean discovery with huge consequences.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX (Costa, Frontera) found the X-ray afterglow, with optical and redshift work by others (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Kulkarni and others). The credited list omits some key figures, so allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and mature after nearly three decades, so recognition is overdue by timing but contested on credit.
uncertainties: Credit for the optical afterglow and redshift discovery is spread among many people.
Late timing and the death of some key contributors.
